facts.text: Every industry checked—aerospace, medical devices, nuclear, rail and automotive—has a simulation credibility framework.
facts.quote: Every industry checked (aerospace, medical devices, nuclear, rail, automotive) has a credibility framework

facts.text: The credibility frameworks checked across aerospace, medical devices, nuclear, rail and automotive agree on a core set: a defined question and context of use, credibility effort scaled to the risk of a wrong decision, verification, validation against physical data, quantified uncertainty, independent review and a documented validity envelope.
facts.quote: a defined question and context of use, credibility effort scaled to the risk of a wrong decision, verification, validation against physical data, quantified uncertainty, independent review and a documented validity envelope

facts.text: None of the credibility frameworks checked across aerospace, medical devices, nuclear, rail and automotive prescribes a universal physical-test percentage or a universal tolerance.
facts.quote: None prescribes a universal physical-test percentage or a universal tolerance (Chapter 10).

facts.text: Simulation agreement is measured with several metrics at once, never with one number.
facts.quote: Agreement is measured with several metrics at once, never one number.

facts.text: Transferring a validated simulation model to another machine model or sensor position is validation-domain extension by similarity plus bridging evidence, not inheritance of validation.
facts.quote: Transfer to another machine model or sensor position is validation-domain extension by similarity plus bridging evidence, not inheritance

facts.text: Validation-domain extension to new machine or sensor-position variants uses a parameterized family model validated at the corners of the envelope, with targeted bridge tests for each new variant.
facts.quote: a parameterized family model validated at the corners of the envelope, with targeted bridge tests for each new variant.

facts.text: Field history from an existing warning system can validate simulation inputs and sub-models, but cannot validate the new closed-loop braking chain.
facts.quote: Field history from the existing warning system can validate inputs and sub-models, not the new closed-loop braking chain.

facts.text: Columbia's debris model is the canonical false-confidence case and provides a lesson about extrapolation outside the validated domain.
facts.quote: The canonical false-confidence case, Columbia's debris model, is a lesson about extrapolation outside the validated domain (Chapter 10).

facts.text: Decision makers and assessors expect a fixed simulation reporting set: a best estimate, an uncertainty statement, a factor-by-factor credibility assessment, a declared validity envelope, separate calibration, validation and withheld confirmation data, and failed validation cases retained in the record.
facts.quote: a best estimate, an uncertainty statement, a factor-by-factor credibility assessment, a declared envelope, separate calibration, validation and withheld confirmation data, and failed validation cases kept in the record
